Ordinal 15 tail-forwards its r0 (`return func_ov062_02117994(c, 3);`) where decl_common.h correctly types it void; ordinal 16 passes a third argument, and the cartridge really does leave r2=1 live across the call at 0x2118110 (mov r2,#1 at 0x2118100, str r2,[r4,#0x38c] at 0x211810c). Both are spelled through namespace views of the same linker symbol (cv_ret, cv_arg3) rather than by overloading the global declaration -- the idiom the sibling oracle ov062/Chuckya uses for func_ov002_020db54c.

byte-diff resolutions, both from writer.md's own catalogue and both measured: (1) func_ov062_02118588 came out 0x19c against the ROM's 0x190 -- bool widening. As C, `int t = (x == 0x11d); if (t != 0)` gave the cartridge's moveq/movne/cmp/movne; as C++ the comparison is a bool and re-testing it costs an extra movne #1 / moveq #0 / cmp #0. Rewritten as a plain if/else. (2) func_ov062_021179e4 differed in 14 words at the same 0x58 -- argument evaluation order. The cartridge loads y, z, x in that order, which is the three-argument constructor the legacy shard used; types.h's Vector3 has no such constructor, and NEITHER three member stores NOR aggregate initialisation reproduces it (both were measured at 14 words differing). A layout-identical local V3ctor with that constructor, handed to Spawn through a reference cast, does.

PROMOTION BLOCKER, measured and single: 11 of the 13 compiler_only_output rows license cleanly; _ZTI5Koopa and _ZTS5Koopa do not. apply_compiler_only_policy (tools/tubuild.py:2280) resolves a row's ROM home through all_symbol_homes(), which is keyed on the symbols.txt SPELLING, not on the address -- and no symbols.txt names _ZTI5Koopa or _ZTS5Koopa. The records exist: ov062 carries _ZTI8daNknk_c at 0x211da68 and _ZTS8daNknk_c at 0x211da5c. Only the class's COINED name breaks the lookup. tubuild.py's own comment at :2264 says so and names the remedy: rename the class to the cartridge's RTTI spelling. Note the asymmetry with _ZTV5Koopa, which DOES resolve: someone added a coined alias row for the vtable, and that is honest because a vtable's bytes do not encode the class name. The same trick is NOT available for _ZTS: this TU emits the string "5Koopa" (0x7 bytes) where the cartridge has "8daNknk_c" (0xa), so an alias row would assert an identity the bytes contradict. The rows are left as deadstrip-data because that is what they factually are -- homed records in this TU's own module -- rather than moved to externalized_output/canonical-import, which would falsely claim the surviving copy lives in another module, or to a plain deadstrip, which tubuild rejects outright for RTTI records precisely because a coined name fakes that claim.

NEXT STEP, and it is NOT part of this promotion: rename Koopa -> daNknk_c. tools/class_rename.py refuses to do it unattended -- `REFUSING: _ZTV8daNknk_c is already defined in config/arm9/overlays/ov062/symbols.txt; a class that already carries the ROM name needs the COINED ALIAS DELETED, not this rename`. So the operation is: delete the _ZTV5Koopa alias row, then run the tool. It rewrites symbols.txt, delinks.txt, include/Koopa.h -> include/daNknk_c.h, BrickBlock.h, this TU and the ledgers, and it changes the class identity the queue, the claim and the remaining pipeline stages address this work by. That is a separate unit of work with its own hazards (mangled length prefixes, ledger row order), not something to fold into a source move -- the same reason linkcheck refuses a near-miss recovery and a promotion in one commit.

SUPERSEDES config/tu_manifest.d/ov062/Koopa+KoopaSmall.json and src_tu/actors/Koopa+KoopaSmall.cpp, both deleted in the same commit. That entry claimed the IDENTICAL .text range 0x21174cc..0x211975c with the same 39 functions -- independent confirmation that the queue's shard_count of 37 is a floor -- but it stopped with `functions_occur_in_expected_order: PARTIAL -- ordinal pair(s) not in ROM order: [(0, 1)]` (the D1/D0 pair, i.e. no defer_codegen off) and compiler_only_output null. Two manifest entries claiming one .text run is a defect in its own right. Its promoted_source also carried a '+' in the filename, which an LCF cannot express.

compiler_only_output.reason: GENUINELY HOMELESS -- no address in any module's symbols.txt carries this name, and the cartridge emits no D2 for this class at all: ov062 has _ZN5KoopaD1Ev at 0x21174cc and _ZN5KoopaD0Ev at 0x2117514 and then goes straight on to func_ov062_02117570 at 0x2117570, with no gap for a third variant. The D2 exists only because Koopa.h declares the destructor out of line, which is the form that reproduces the cartridge's D1-below-D0 order under `#pragma defer_codegen off` (out-of-line + deferred codegen emits D2, D0, D1 -- the wrong way round). Plain `deadstrip`, not `deadstrip-duplicate`: there is no ROM copy to be a duplicate of.

This TU odr-uses Vector3 as a FUNCTION LOCAL in four members (ordinals 3, 4, 6 and 19) and has no Vector3 data member; the emitted symbol is one vague-linkage copy however many objects there are.

This TU owns the key function (the out-of-line destructor at ordinal 0), so it emits the class vtable. STORAGE 0x84 = 0x211daac..0x211db30; SYMBOL EXTENT from the address point 0x211dab4 = 0x7c = 31 words. The two differ by the 8-byte offset-to-top + typeinfo preamble.
